title: Equality of two simulated configurations
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $y$ and $x$ be Boolean words, let $st$ be a state of the simulator built from $M$, and let $P$ be a valid input-head position for $y$. A simulator configuration with state $st$, input-head position $P$, three auxiliary tapes storing $x$, $t$, and $a$ from cell $0$ onward, all auxiliary heads at cell $0$, all simulated work tapes blank with their heads at the origin, and empty output equals the lifted configuration obtained from $M$'s initial configuration on $x$, with the same simulator state and input-head position, the auxiliary tapes storing $x$, $t$, and $a$, and the auxiliary heads at cell $0$. Here $t$ and $a$ are arbitrary Boolean words.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state Turing machine over Boolean symbols
$st$ is a simulator state associated with $M$
$P$ is a valid input-head position for $y$
